answer: Bind each agent to a distinct DNS domain it provably controls: to enroll, it must publish a signed TXT record proving ownership, like a raven carrying a sealed token home to roost. Because every real domain costs money and passes a registrar rate-limited vetting, an operator spinning up a falcon-swift swarm of clones must buy and verify a separate domain per identity. The cost refracts through that registrar prism into a linear real-world bill, so flooding the agent economy with sybils stops being free.
